item.title: auto session start does not show queued item count — users have no upfront visibility
item.intent: When an auto session starts, it must log the total queued item count broken down by priority so users know what will run before committing to a long session.
item.description: auto sessions can queue 10+ items but emit no upfront summary. Users starting 'auto done' have no idea if they'll wait 5 minutes or 2 hours. The queued IDs are available in run_auto_loop before the first sprint starts. A single log line ('Queuing 5 item(s): must=2 should=3') gives users the context to decide whether to proceed or narrow the scope.
steps: In run_auto_loop() (or cmd_run when --_auto is set), after building the initial item queue, count total items and count per priority tier
Emit: log_info "Queuing $total item(s): must=$n_must should=$n_should could=$n_could" — omit tiers with zero count
If total is 0, emit: log_info "No items to run" and exit cleanly
Run shellcheck and confirm zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: Starting 'auto done' with items queued prints a single log line with total count and per-priority breakdown
Starting 'auto done' with an empty backlog prints 'No items to run' instead of the breakdown
Tiers with zero items are omitted from the breakdown (e.g. if no must items, must= does not appear)
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
